test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Booker-shortlisted Indian novel from 2008 examines the Bhopal gas tragedy through allegory?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Animal's People**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Animal's People**, authored by **Indra Sinha**, is a poignant novel that uses **allegory** to recount the devastating **1984 Bhopal gas tragedy**.
 
• The novel is set in the fictional city of **Khaufpur** (derived from the Urdu word for **terror**), which serves as a stand-in for **Bhopal**, capturing the visceral reality of industrial negligence.
 
• The story is narrated by **Animal**, a nineteen-year-old protagonist whose spine was severely twisted by the toxic fumes released during **'That Night'**, forcing him to walk on all fours like a beast.
 
• The central conflict involves the struggle of the **Khaufpuris** against the **Kampani**, a thinly veiled representation of the **Union Carbide Corporation**, which avoids legal accountability for the disaster.
 
• Although the book was shortlisted for the **Man Booker Prize** in **2007**, it achieved significant literary milestones in **2008**, including winning the **Commonwealth Writers' Prize** for Best Book in the Europe and South Asia region.
 
• The narrative structure is unique, presented as a series of **tape recordings** made by Animal for a journalist, providing a raw and unfiltered perspective on **disability**, **poverty**, and **corporate exploitation**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **The White Tiger**:
 
 
• Written by **Aravind Adiga**, this novel won the **Man Booker Prize** in **2008**.
 
• It follows the journey of **Balram Halwai** and offers a satirical look at the **class struggle** and **economic disparity** in modern India.
 
 
 
• **Sea of Poppies**:
 
 
• Written by **Amitav Ghosh**, this novel was shortlisted for the **Man Booker Prize** in **2008**.
 
• It is the first installment of the **Ibis Trilogy**, focusing on the **opium trade** between British India and China.
 
 
 
• **The Ministry of Utmost Happiness**:
 
 
• This **2017** novel by **Arundhati Roy** was longlisted for the **Man Booker Prize**.
 
• It weaves together diverse narratives involving the **Kashmir conflict** and the lives of **transgender characters** (Hijras) in Delhi.
